claim.quote: The exposure-dependent single-electron rate (SER) of one of these sensors was measured $\sim$100~m underground, yielding $(1.8\pm 0.3)\times10^{-3}~e^-$/pix/day at 131K.

name: Studying single-electron traps in newly fabricated Skipper-CCDs for the Oscura experiment using the pocket-pumping technique
notes: Detector R&D measurement on prototype sensors, not an Oscura dark matter search.

summary.plain: Oscura's first batches of sensors were studied for tiny defects that can fake a one-electron signal. One sensor, measured about 100 m underground, showed a single-electron rate of about two thousandths per pixel per day.
summary.technical: Pocket-pumping measurements of energy and cross section of defects/contaminants in buried-channel regions of three Oscura prototype skipper-CCDs from different fabrication batches; the type of defects is more closely linked to the batch than to the gettering method; SER of one sensor measured ~100 m underground at 131 K.

title: Studying single-electron traps in newly fabricated Skipper-CCDs for the Oscura experiment using the pocket-pumping technique
why_it_matters: The abstract concludes that the exposure-dependent single-electron rate of Oscura prototype sensors would be lower in lower-background environments.
